q: A user sees another person's notes. Which test would have caught it?
o: A rules test where Bob reads Alice's note and fails
why: Security rules tests in the emulator should include one user trying to read another user's note.

q: Your bill doubled the day after a release. What do you check first?
o: Unlimited list queries and self-triggering functions
why: Reads on whole collections and functions that trigger themselves in a loop are the usual causes of sudden cost.

q: After you enforce App Check, many users get errors. What went wrong?
o: Enforcement came before most requests were verified
why: Watch App Check metrics first; enforce only when most requests are verified.

q: Reminders stopped for one user but reach everyone else. Likely cause?
o: A stale token or removed permission
why: If others get messages, the send works; that one device's token or permission is the problem. See the send errors.

q: A user deletes their account. What else must go?
o: Their notes, photos and users/{uid} data with tokens
why: Account deletion should remove all their data, which a function can do in one place.

q: When should you set a budget alert?
o: The day you move to Blaze
why: Costs can start as soon as you are on Blaze, which may be at the photo upload step.

q: Where should you build and test steps 1 to 4?
why: The emulator is free and keeps test data away from real users and your bill.

q: A new client needs monthly SQL reports across all customers. Best move?
o: A live listener on every collection
An analytics database or SQL Connect
why: Reports across many records need SQL; Firestore has no joins in its standard edition and bills per read.

q: A budget alert stops your project from spending more than the budget.
why: A budget alert only warns you by email; it does not stop spending.

q: Push messages cannot be fully tested in the Emulator Suite, so you test the send with a real device.
why: There is no Cloud Messaging emulator; deploy the function and check that the phone gets the notification.
